about: Tasks to try the skill on, in the same shape as the vendored nuvui evals: a one-line prompt, the packages installed, and regular expressions for what the written files should and shouldn't contain. A match is a first look only; the result still has to pass `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @repo/db test` and `pnpm db:check`.

evals.prompt: Add a posts table: each post has an author (a user), a title, a body, an optional publish date, and timestamps. Users can have many posts.

expect.why: One table per file under src/schema.
snakeCase.table keeps column names written once.
The foreign key column is indexed.
A migration is generated, not hand-written or pushed.

reject.why: Column names written twice instead of snakeCase.table.
The v1 relations() API, not defineRelations.
push is for throwaway local databases only.
text, unless a real limit exists.

evals.prompt: Write a query that returns the 10 authors with the most published posts in the last 30 days, with their post count.

expect.why: Aggregates use the select builder, not RQB.
Query functions take the executor first.

reject.why: Counting in JavaScript after fetching every row.
RQB has no groupBy; use the select builder.

evals.prompt: Add a function that moves credits from one account to another and sends a notification email afterwards.

expect.why: Both updates happen in one transaction.
The writes go through tx, not db.
Writes return what the caller needs.

reject.why: Slow I/O inside the transaction holds locks and a connection.
Named prepared statements break behind PgBouncer transaction pooling.
